free_tier.stated: no free storage quota is stated on the landing page; the product is sold as a private cloud drive with a cloud-download engine

per_object_cap.stated: not established; the pricing page is served as a non-HTML body that the reader refused

egress.terms: not established; recorded as metered:false because no per-GB price or cap was found, which is an absence of evidence and not evidence of absence

tooling: unofficial drivers only; the product's value is server-side torrent and magnet download into the drive, not an open API
chaining: a cloud-download engine rather than a store: it fetches a magnet to its own disk, which is useful for acquiring a corpus and not for holding one
reliability_note: The pricing page is served as a binary body, so its plan table could not be read through the reader; the landing page states the cloud-download speed claim without a quota.

evidence.proved: the landing page describes a private cloud drive with a cloud-download server and claims 'more than 80% of the files can be downloaded to your PikPak private Cloud Drive within a few seconds'; it states no storage quota
the reader refused the page as 'not-html:binary' and the fetch broker returned a compressed binary body, so the plan table could not be read; this is why the record is unverified

notes: Recorded to close the survey, not to recommend. The landing page states that more than 80% of files can be downloaded to the drive in seconds through the cloud-download server, and that is a claim about acquisition rather than storage. No quota, cap, retention or egress term was obtained: mypikpak.com/en/price returns a body the reader classified as non-HTML, and the fetch broker returned binary. This is the honest gap, not a finding.

extras.blocked: pricing page served as a binary body

binding_note: Nothing numeric could be established first-hand, so the record names the cap as the thing that would decide and records it as unestablished.
